card.line: Syria, called Aram in the Old Testament, was the land north of Israel. Its kings fought Israel and Judah, and in the New Testament news of Jesus spread there.

moments.title: Naaman the commander
moments.text: Naaman, the commander of the king of Aram's army, was a great man, but he had leprosy. A young girl taken from Israel told his wife about the prophet in Samaria, and the king sent Naaman to Israel with a letter and gifts.

moments.title: Aram's king hunts Elisha
moments.text: The king of Aram was at war with Israel, but Elisha kept warning Israel's king where the Arameans would go. The angry king sent a great army to surround Elisha at Dothan, but the LORD struck the Arameans with blindness.

moments.title: Elisha and Hazael in Damascus
moments.text: Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad, king of Aram, was sick. Hazael brought a gift and asked if the king would recover. Elisha said the LORD had shown him that Hazael would be king over Aram.

moments.title: Aram plots against Judah
moments.text: Rezin, king of Aram, marched against Jerusalem with Israel's king Pekah. The LORD sent Isaiah to tell Ahaz not to be afraid, because the plot against Judah would not happen.

moments.title: Jesus' fame spreads
moments.text: News about Jesus spread all over Syria. People brought Him all who were ill, in pain, demon-possessed, having seizures, or paralyzed, and He healed them.
